Block questions: the expert's audit disagreed on 1 of 10 sampled agreements (10 %, above the 5 % trigger), so every agreed block question gets the expert's full review. The expert review of eval plan §5.3 (H1b) reviews all 100 block questions after the decided template edits; its verdicts enter reviews/block_questions.jsonl as full-review audit rows on the 81 agreed rows not in the sample, and none differs from the agreed value.

Block questions: the decided edits are template edits (the port base, the interleaver mapping, the rounding rule, an exact tolerance for the patterned interleaver). They reach 22 of the 100 questions; the rebuilt set keeps the same 100 ids, settings and answers, and the 22 carry `approved-with-edits`.

Calculation answers: on 5 of the 7 questions the script's key classed as underspecified, both blind recomputations and the expert found one answer; the expert's value is the confirmed reference (items/tier_k/test/calc_answers.jsonl, `confirmed`). 2 stay underspecified, as do 2 more on which both recomputations agreed with the key.

Twin thresholds: the decided labels give 0.92 (semantic) and 0.55 (lexical), the thresholds in use; the dev split and the training-team exclusions do not change. The lexical band [0.60, 0.70) has 12 twins of 32, below half, between two bands above half.

Rubrics, automatic checks before the checkers: all 292 writer rows parse, are accepted by the judge's rubric code and the rule cascade, quote every GNU Radio source line exactly, and give full credit to the confirmed calculations; 21 dev rubrics share one or more word 8-grams with a teacher answer to the question and go to the expert agent as `checks failed`, whatever the checkers decide.

Rubrics, theory sources: textbook and standard section numbers cannot be checked against a local file. The dev writer marked some as given from memory; the checkers were told to look each one up and report a wrong citation as an edit.

Tier A: the expert rejected 7 tasks (gba-dev-08, gba-dev-09, gba-test-06, gba-test-07, gba-test-21, gba-test-22, gba-test-23) as trivially short and padded to reach 8 tool calls (checklist B); on three it reproduced a wrong answer passing. The Tier-A test set has 25 tasks, and its knowledge category has no test task left; both are reported with the removals (eval plan §5.3).

Tier A: the decided edits are applied as patches (reviews/tier_a_patches.json) by the generators, plus one generator-wide change (every File Sink file constraint is a base-name regex). The grader gains two decided features, answer.forbid (refusal tasks must not claim success) and files[].oracle (a measured range on a written file), so GRADER_VERSION is grcbench.tier_a.grader/2 and every Tier-A gate is re-run.

Tier F group 1: the expert's audit disagreed on at least 3 of its 5 sampled agreements, above the 5 % trigger, so every agreed task of the group gets the expert's full review. The expert review of eval plan §5.3 (H1b) reviews every Tier-F task after the decided edits; its verdicts enter reviews/tier_f.jsonl as full-review audit rows, and none differs from the agreed value.

Tier F group 3: reviewer 1 (a10) started about 40 minutes before reviewer 2 (a13), because a usage-limit stop left one slot free at a time; neither sees the other's output, so the reviews stay independent. Both, like the expert, were told the generator issues the group 1 and 2 reviewers had found.

Usage limit: the review agents stopped twice on the claude.ai usage limit (Fri 13 Nov about 23:00 to Sat 14 Nov 19:00), and once when the session closed; every row written before a stop is kept, and the stopped agents were resumed under their own declared numbers.

Tier F group 2: the expert's audit disagreed on 1 of its 5 sampled agreements (gbf-test-16: both reviewers approved; the expert found that an answer with no channelizer passes and decided four path checks), above the 5 % trigger, so the agreed tasks of group 2 also get the expert's full review, done by the expert review of eval plan §5.3 (H1b) of every Tier-F task: its verdicts enter reviews/tier_f.jsonl as full-review audit rows on every agreed row, and none differs from the agreed value.

Contamination, Tier-K test: the expert's audit disagreed on 1 of its 18 sampled agreements (q_90ea1e7c7eadbe00 against a devstral teacher answer: both reviewers found it contaminated; the expert found the item's GNU Radio half absent from the training text), above the 5 % trigger, so the expert reviews every other agreed row of the sheet (162 rows) blind, as audit rows. The other three contamination sheets had no audit disagreement.

Tier A categories: the review rejected all three knowledge test tasks, two of the three save_block test tasks and the dev task of each of the two categories (knowledge gba-test-06, 21, 22 and gba-dev-08; save_block gba-test-07, 23 and gba-dev-09): a competent agent needs one to three calls for them, and their golden sequences reach the 8-call floor of eval plan §4.4 only with filler calls. The test split therefore has no knowledge task and one save_block task, against the Tier-A checklist's rule that every category has a test task. The expert review (H1b) confirmed the rejections. Tier-A results are reported for the categories that remain (pre-registration §10).

Rubrics: the expert agent (a25) opened public pysdr.org pages (plain page reads; nothing was sent) to check PySDR section titles, the Pluto firmware commands of q_e3e6604e987b8042 and the spectrogram axes of q_3a07b91fa273b2e5, all dev questions; where a book chapter could not be checked locally it cites the source by content. Seven of its merged dev rubrics shared word 8-grams with a teacher answer (mostly standard formulas); the import refused them, the expert re-worded the flagged lines with the same content, and all seven then passed.

Expert review (H1b) of the Tier-K GNU Radio questions: four `accept with edits`. Two dev rubrics get the expert's rewritten P1 (q_8c9b8bb7a2fa6c35: GRC 3.10.12 names the generated file after the ID that Save As sets; q_8a85a884de1f5695: the DC Blocker block also earns P1), through reviews/rubric_dev_patches.json. Tier F was reviewed in three groups of about 65 tasks, so its audit sample was drawn per group: 10 %, at least 5 agreed rows of each group, ordered by SHA-256 of the seed, `tier_f/g<group>` and the row. Groups 1 and 2 called for a full review, which the expert review (H1b) of every task gives.

Rubrics: a rubric that both checkers reject goes to the expert, who rewrites it (a checker's reject means 'wrong in a way that needs rewriting'). One dev question was affected, q_ae75402a9c841093: the writer marked it underspecified, both checkers found it answerable, and the expert wrote its rubric.

Second round (the replacement tasks, agents 31 to 36): of the 27 Tier-F replacements, both reviewers rejected 6 as duplicates of first-round tasks of their cells (gbf-test-151, -153, -154, -156, -164 and gbf-dev-48: the same edit on the other tone, or another parameter of the same tune, as the ladder showed both ways). The expert agent decided 8 rows (6 with merged edits, 2 approve), its audit agreed on all 5 sampled agreements, and its expert review accepted the other 21. The two Tier-A reviewers asked for different edits on all 9 Tier-A replacements, so the expert agent decided all 9 (approve with edits), and its expert review accepted all 9. The coordinator re-ran all 99 ladder runs the Tier-F reviewers recorded, and every one gave the claimed rung.

Second round, the decided edits: the Tier-F edits are patches (reviews/tier_f_patches.json), except gbf-test-155's instruction, which the generator writes (its quantizer phrase names the Short To Float scale of the graph it describes); the Tier-A edits are in grcbench.tier_a.replacements. Four of the six repeat an edit on another instance of the same block type (tone_1 and tone_2, or a square and a sawtooth source), which the generator's shared-cell rule keys on the block type and parameter (edit_key). gbf-dev-48 and gbf-test-154 tune another block of the same chain to the same output; the rule does not see that kind of duplicate, and the review removed both. Every edited task passes its gates and golden replay (10/10), and every shortcut graph a reviewer or the coordinator built for a fault the edits correct fails V5.

Edits after the review (pre-registration §10, the team's decision of 17 November): the replacements' two graph checks on 7 first-round Tier-F build tasks (gbf-test-24, -37, -94, -114, -134, -135, gbf-dev-33), and the replacements' reply order in gba-test-24, as patches marked post_review; grader version 4 (a regex parameter constraint also matches the evaluated value) for the 15 first-round Tier-A file-name checks.
